description: Shared instructions respect project-owned files and configuration instead of imposing the Domios development repository.

evals.name: project-agents-file-is-not-generated-home-file
evals.prompt: Dry run; no tools. The user explicitly asks you to add one short rule to D:/Projects/invoice-app/AGENTS.md. It is a checked-in file owned by that unrelated project, and that project's instructions permit this requested edit. This is not the Domios General Agent home directory. Would you perform the edit or refuse? Explain briefly. Also say whether the same permission applies to the instruction files Domios regenerates in its General Agent home. Do not claim to have edited anything.
evals.expected_output: Allows the authorized project edit while protecting only generated General Agent home instructions.
expectations: Agrees to perform the explicitly authorized project-owned AGENTS.md edit; does not refuse because all files with that name are supposedly generated by Domios.
Keeps the restriction on Domios-generated General Agent home instruction files; does not extend the project permission to those generated files.

evals.name: instance-identity-is-not-a-hardcoded-port
evals.prompt: Dry run; no tools. You need to identify which Domios installation is the active production instance before planning work on a separate disposable test instance. The owner has customized the installation configuration, and no port numbers have been supplied. What do you rely on to identify production, and may you kill it? Answer briefly without executing or inventing discovery results.
evals.expected_output: Uses actual instance configuration and preserves production without guessing the repository's development ports.
expectations: Requires actual installation/configuration or verified instance evidence rather than assigning a fixed production or development port.
Does not kill or plan to kill the active production Domios instance.

evals.name: cartographer-follows-assigned-project-budget
evals.prompt: Dry run; no tools. You are documenting an unrelated scheduling product. The owner-approved project contract sets a map budget of 180 nodes and allows source citations in detailed normative documents. A valid proposed map has 130 nodes. Must you reduce it below 100, forbid source citations, or impose Domios source layout? State what you would preserve and check; do not generate files or claim validation ran.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the actual project's budget, link policy and domain instead of imposing the Domios repository's conventions.
expectations: Accepts 130 nodes within the supplied 180-node budget; does not impose an assumed approximately 100-node cap.
Follows the supplied project's citation policy and layout without forbidding all source links or imposing Domios agents/providers/Service architecture.
Still requires the map to reflect the project's authorized product contracts; does not treat size or structural validity alone as semantic proof.
